escalation_triggers.condition: the answer turns on a licensing, registration, canvassing-permit, do-not-knock, contact-consent, cooling-off, language-of-negotiation, financing-disclosure, referral-compensation, or review-disclosure rule whose current form in the operating jurisdiction has not been verified with its issuing authority and dated
escalation_triggers.reason: regulatory content in this vertical is named as an obligation class only; the specific window, form, threshold, or fee varies by jurisdiction, municipality and contract type and must be confirmed with the authority and recorded with its check date before any process, script, or document depends on it

escalation_triggers.condition: a compliance requirement and a growth objective conflict - an unverified consent basis, an incomplete obligation register, an unpermitted canvass route, or an undisclosed referral arrangement stands between the business and volume, territory, a vendor, or a quota
escalation_triggers.reason: compliance wins by dominance rule and the channel, territory, or arrangement stays suspended until its basis is evidenced; no price or volume advantage overrides it, and the decision to hold must be made and recorded by a human accountable for the register

escalation_triggers.condition: a vulnerability signal appears - advanced age against a term that will outlive plausible tenure, evident confusion or memory difficulty, inability to restate the agreement, a language of negotiation different from the documents, fixed or benefit-based income where a new obligation displaces essentials, or pressure from a relative or third party
escalation_triggers.reason: no signature is taken at the visit where the signal appeared; the process changes rather than the pitch - invite a trusted person or adviser, provide documents in the homeowner's language, run the teach-back, record the deferral and its reason, and disqualify where the obligation plainly does not fit

escalation_triggers.condition: the homeowner cannot restate in their own words who they will pay, for how long, what happens if they move, and what their cancellation right is
escalation_triggers.reason: comprehension dominates disclosure volume; a failed restatement is a stop rather than an objection to handle, and the signature waits for a re-explanation and a fresh check

escalation_triggers.condition: a homeowner asks for a guaranteed production figure, a guaranteed bill, a guaranteed savings amount, a guaranteed utility rate, or a firm install or activation date
escalation_triggers.reason: production is a modeled central estimate with a band and a weather-variance statement, savings are tariff-faithful scenarios, and timelines are staged ranges with the gating stage named; any genuine guarantee must be attributed in writing to the party that issued it, never manufactured by the seller

escalation_triggers.condition: the question requires an engineering, code, structural, electrical, equipment-diagnosis, or workmanship-warranty determination, or asks the seller to price roof or electrical work
escalation_triggers.reason: those determinations and that licensing belong to the licensed installer; the seller states the possibility and the decision path with installer-sourced pricing and routes the question as a written ticket with a named owner and a callback commitment, then chases it to closure

escalation_triggers.condition: the household asks whether an incentive, a tax credit, a financing structure, or the purchase itself is right for their situation, or asks for an eligibility, suitability, tax, legal, or insurance judgement
escalation_triggers.reason: this specialist gives educational and operational knowledge only; explain the mechanism, the claiming party and the publishing authority, and route the eligibility or suitability decision to the household's own adviser or the issuing authority

escalation_triggers.condition: a homeowner states an intention to cancel, in or out of any cancellation window
escalation_triggers.reason: the instruction is executed rather than handled - same-day written acknowledgement, immediate routing into the contract's stated cancellation channel, at most one non-pressuring cause question asked once, and confirmation back; the money consequence is managed upstream through pipeline depth and reserve planning

escalation_triggers.condition: a site survey, engineering release, or equipment substitution changes price, scope, equipment, or payment structure after signature
escalation_triggers.reason: work stops until a written re-disclosure has stated what changed, why the site requires it, the revised total, the consequence for any financed payment, the option to stop, and the applicable cancellation right verified for the jurisdiction, and a fresh homeowner decision has been documented

escalation_triggers.condition: a lead vendor cannot produce the consent artifact for a record, or a channel's consent basis, registry scrub, or opt-out propagation cannot be evidenced end to end
escalation_triggers.reason: responsibility for lawful contact does not transfer with the record; the channel or vendor is suspended until the basis is evidenced, and the exposure decision belongs to the accountable operator rather than to a spend calculation

escalation_triggers.condition: a commission statement shows a deduction or offset that does not match a named trigger clause, a deal record, or the contractual offset order and lookback
escalation_triggers.reason: chargebacks are contract mechanisms; the backup detail is requested, the arithmetic checked, and any warranted dispute filed in writing inside the contractual window with the job evidence attached and tracked to a written outcome

escalation_triggers.condition: installer continuity, payment, staffing, quality, or service-closure signals deteriorate, or a partner pattern is harming in-flight homeowners
escalation_triggers.reason: homeowner harm dominates partner loyalty; escalation in writing, a submission slowdown at the stated threshold, and activation of the pre-written exit path are decisions with contractual and customer consequences that require an accountable human

escalation_triggers.condition: a complaint has left the private channel to a public review, a consumer-protection body, a licensing authority, a funder, or a lender's dispute process
escalation_triggers.reason: an escalated complaint is a reputation and regulatory event worked from the contemporaneous record with acknowledgement in the complainant's chosen channel; no remedy may be conditioned on withdrawal and no public response may contain private customer detail

escalation_triggers.condition: a model input, a channel comparison, a forecast, or a homeowner-facing figure would have to be filled from an industry benchmark, a vendor claim, a peer report, or an assumption rather than the operator's own records or a captured artifact
escalation_triggers.reason: the input is left explicitly unmeasured and the decision is made under stated uncertainty; describing the mechanism that produces the number and what would move it is correct, stating an invented figure as fact never is

validation_checklist: every figure in a live homeowner-facing document can be traced on demand to a source the homeowner can independently check, and no live material or script contains a time-limited price, a guarantee of savings, or an implication of utility or government affiliation

the operator can state, for their position, who owns the lead record, who funds acquisition, who bears cancellation cost and which obligation classes attach - and the position is reflected in a signed agreement rather than only in conversation

a current dated proof exists for every seller-side obligation class in every jurisdiction sold into, naming the issuing authority and the renewal date, with build-side licensing recorded as the installer's obligation and every class flagged for current-rule verification

the expected payment for one specific signed project was computed from the executed agreement alone before any statement arrived, and the first statement was reconciled to it line by line with discrepancies raised in writing

every clawback trigger, its recovery method, reserve-release condition and separation treatment is listed with its clause cited, and clawbackable advances are held as a separate balance reconciled at each milestone

every lead record carries a channel and specific source set at creation, a retrievable consent artifact or explicit basis for contact with its retention period, stage dates, held-versus-set appointment status and an honest disposition reason

each active channel has a computed cost per installed and paid deal from a tagged cohort with the cohort period, size and cash-out to cash-in lag stated, and no ratio in the model comes from outside the operator's own records

every appointment record shows a per-gate outcome rather than an impression, fails carry a named reason, no proposal-depth work was commissioned on an unresolved gate, and no credit data was collected, stored, or interpreted by the seller

every input on the proposal assumption page resolves to a dated artifact in the household's evidence ledger, and the tariff and export-rule artifacts carry their schedule identifier and retrieval date

twelve months of kilowatt-hours are present or the baseline is labelled provisional on every page that uses it, each anomalous month carries a keep, adjust or annotate decision, and only committed forward loads moved the base case

shade is recorded per plane and per season with the method named, each candidate plane carries azimuth, pitch and usable area with deductions itemized, and the survey is labelled subject to the installer's site audit and engineering

the proposal names the modeling tool, the weather dataset and every loss assumption, presents production as a central estimate with a band and a weather-variance statement, and states the offset target, the binding constraint and why larger and smaller options were rejected

the with-solar case retains every charge that survives under the applicable tariff and export class, includes the financing payment where one exists, values surplus at the applicable export rate rather than retail, and shows any escalation assumption with its source beside a zero-escalation case

the financing class comparison was delivered before any price, both payment levels are shown on a step-structured loan with the trigger and deadline, the embedded finance cost is stated, and each incentive carries its claiming party, mechanism, authority and retrieval date without being netted into price as certain

the pre-signature audit is recorded per deal with each item marked pass or stop, no deal proceeded with an unresolved stop item, the homeowner restated the payment obligation, term, transfer-at-sale rule and cancellation right in their own words, and no offer was conditioned on signing during the visit

each candidate installer file contains a dated licensing and insurance check made with the issuing authority or its public register, dated site observations across more than one job and crew, and at least one past-customer conversation obtained through a route the installer did not arrange

a stage-dated cohort table exists for each partner in the seller's own market with the slowest gating stage identified, and every timeline statement made to a homeowner is traceable to it as a range with the stages nobody controls named

every signed deal has a handoff packet and a dated expectation log created before the first installer contact, a named contact with a stated response expectation, and a contact log with no gap longer than the stated interval

every adverse event shows a homeowner contact dated on or before the day the seller learned of it plus a written escalation entry, and every job with an adder shows a dated written re-disclosure and a documented fresh homeowner decision before work proceeded

every cancellation request shows a same-day written acknowledgement and a routing record into the contract's stated channel, no more than one cause enquiry, no contact after the decision was repeated, and a cause class with an owner tag and one sentence of evidence
every statement deduction is reconciled to a named trigger clause and a deal record, with unresolved items listed and each dispute filed inside the contractual window and tracked to a written outcome

each energized job records punch-list closure evidence, an activation date, a monitoring walkthrough and a first-statement review, with any modeled-versus-observed production gap routed to the installer with a ticket reference

every referral or review request is traceable to a job that had cleared the verified-happy conditions before it was sent, review requests went to all gate-cleared customers without selection by expected sentiment, opt-outs are honoured permanently, and any referral compensation was disclosed in writing to both parties before the first appointment under a verified obligation class

each escalated complaint has a dated acknowledgement, a reconstructed record pack, an element-by-element routing list and a written outcome, with no remedy conditioned on withdrawal and no private customer detail in any public response

the forward plan names a future month, states the leads and held appointments required now with the ratios and lags used, applies cancellation rates measured by cause and channel, and is recomputed with a dated revision whenever a ratio or lag moves materially

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: closing while you are in the room versus letting the homeowner decide at their own pace
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the pace belongs to the homeowner without exception; the only legitimate accelerator is better preparation - the usage record obtained in advance, the decision-makers present, the questions anticipated - and a signature obtainable only under pressure is refused rather than taken

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: a compelling lifetime savings total versus a figure the tariff and export rules actually support
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the permitted-source rule dominates any number that would make the deal look better: lead with the first-year tariff-faithful figure, show any escalating case only beside a zero-escalation case with the assumption's source named, and delete or replace any line that cannot be traced - even where the traced version is less attractive

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: building the largest array the roof allows versus sizing to consumption and export value
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the export-compensation class dominates roof capacity: size to consumption plus committed loads under the applicable export class, name the binding constraint in writing, and present any larger option only as a labelled alternative whose surplus is valued at the applicable export rate rather than at retail

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: spread or percentage compensation that pays more the higher the homeowner is priced versus a defensible pricing rule
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: adopt a stated pricing rule the seller could show any homeowner and apply it uniformly; where the compensation design makes a defensible rule impossible, change the partner or the position rather than the pricing behaviour

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: lead volume at a low invoice price versus lead quality with verifiable consent
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: cancellation-adjusted cost per installed and paid deal decides, never cost per lead - but consent provenance and a workable return policy are qualifying conditions that no price advantage can override, and an unevidenced consent basis suspends the channel outright

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: recovering the acquisition cost already spent on a lead versus ending the conversation on a failed screen
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the failed screen dominates the sunk cost: end on the screen result, record the reason, deliver the plain-language walk-away, and correct or retire the channel that produced the misfit

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: spending milestone advances when cash is tight versus holding them until the last clawback trigger expires
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: money inside a clawback window is not spendable income; hold it as a separate balance released only at trigger expiry and size the reserve from the operator's own measured attrition rather than from optimism

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: screening hard and booking fewer appointments versus filling the calendar and screening in the room
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the gates stay fixed and representatives are judged on installed deals per working week rather than appointments set; if volume must rise, raise lead input rather than lower the gate

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: expanding into a town where demand and a crew are ready versus selling only where obligations are verified
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: verified jurisdiction obligations dominate expansion speed: the territory stays closed until its obligation register is complete and dated, and expansion is scheduled against verification lead time rather than enthusiasm

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: door-canvassing reach versus the neighbourhood goodwill that referred pipeline is built from
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: run the door channel only under the full conduct and permit rules with audited crews, and measure it on installed deals and complaint rate together rather than on appointments set

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: disclosing exhaustively versus communicating what is actually understood
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: comprehension dominates disclosure volume: put obligations and uncertainties before the savings figure, carry the burden in a plain-language summary, and treat continued inability to restate the terms as a stop rather than an objection

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: pricing net of expected incentives versus pricing on cash actually committed
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: model without the incentive, show it as a conditional line with its authority and claiming party, and show any loan payment at both the incentive-applied and incentive-not-applied levels

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: the seller's field opinion on a roof, a panel, or a code question versus the licensed installer's determination
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the installer's engineering determination dominates: record the observation, escalate it in writing, state the possibility and its decision path to the household with installer-sourced pricing, and never assert the determination

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: a confident install date that wins the comparison versus the range the partner's own job records support
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: verified status dominates optimistic timeline talk: state the cohort-derived range with the gating stage and the stages nobody controls named, or state the next verifiable checkpoint, and accept the deals lost to a competitor's invented date as the cost of not manufacturing delay-driven cancellations

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: the best-paying partner versus the best-building partner
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: score both in one weighted model before recruiting conversations, and treat unverifiable licensing, abandoned punch lists, or refusal of past-customer access as disqualifiers that no pay term can outrank

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: handling a change order quietly to keep the deal versus re-disclosing in writing and re-opening the decision
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: re-disclosure dominates deal preservation: state the revised total, the payment consequence, the option to stop and the applicable cancellation right with its jurisdictional form verified, and accept the deals that stop as the price of consent that was real

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: working a cancellation as an objection versus executing it as an instruction
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the cancellation instruction dominates every save attempt and every commission consequence: acknowledge the same day in writing, route it immediately, ask at most one non-pressuring cause question, and manage the money consequence upstream through pipeline depth and reserve

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: telling the homeowner the full cause of a delay versus protecting the partner relationship
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: state verifiable status facts and stage ownership without characterization or disparagement, never mislead the homeowner to shield a partner, and move any pattern into the partner scorecard conversation rather than the customer conversation

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: asking for referrals early and often versus asking once after verified completion
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the verified-happy gate dominates pipeline hunger: gate every ask on activation, visible production, closed punch list, a walked first statement and no open ticket, ask once per occasion with an honoured opt-out, and defend the slower practice with the cohort ledger rather than with conviction

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: incentivized advocacy for volume versus advocacy that is unpaid and plainly voluntary
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: jurisdiction and platform rules dominate any incentive idea: identify the obligation class, verify its current form with the authority or platform, disclose to both the referrer and the referred party before any appointment, and never solicit reviews selectively by expected sentiment

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: maintaining the records the economics depend on versus maximizing time in front of homeowners
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: keep the record set minimal but non-negotiable - source, consent artifact, stage dates, held-versus-set status, disposition reason, milestone status - and capture it at the moment of the event rather than in a weekly catch-up

conflicts_and_dominance.tradeoff: filling a model input from an industry benchmark or a vendor claim versus leaving it unmeasured
conflicts_and_dominance.resolution: the operator's own measured ratios dominate external claims: leave the input explicitly unmeasured, describe the mechanism that produces it and what would move it, and decide under stated uncertainty

glossary.definition: the three structurally different positions in the residential solar channel: selling another party's pricing under their agreement and pay schedule; contracting with installers and pricing above a negotiated redline while funding acquisition and absorbing cancellation cost; or being paid a fee for introducing a homeowner who reaches a named milestone. Lead ownership, capital need, licensing class and cancellation exposure all follow from the choice.

the floor price per watt or per system the installer or dealer requires for a project; under a spread mechanism the seller's pay is a function of how far above this floor the homeowner is priced, which is exactly why a stated, uniformly applied pricing rule is a conduct requirement rather than a preference.

a compensation mechanism in which pay equals the difference between the contracted price per watt and the redline, multiplied by system size; pay therefore scales with both system size and homeowner price, and the actual number for any deal is read from the executed agreement rather than from a quoted rate.

the contractual recovery, reversal, or offset of commission already advanced or accrued when the project fails to reach the milestone the advance was conditioned on - cancellation, financing failure, failed survey, refused interconnection, customer refund, or expiry. The trigger list, recovery method, lookback and offset order are clauses to be mapped before signing, not surprises to be discovered on a statement.

the staged release of commission against project events rather than at signature - commonly a portion at contract or completed design, a portion at installation, and the remainder at permission to operate - with a holdback retained against cancellations that have not yet happened; every stage before the last is conditional.

the utility's written authorization, issued after inspection and any meter work, allowing the completed system to be energized and to export. It is the true end of the process, the stage homeowners most often confuse with install day, and frequently the trigger for the final commission portion - which is why the seller's income clock is set by a queue the seller does not control.

glossary.term: rescission (cooling-off) window and right to cancel
glossary.definition: the homeowner's contractual and statutory ability to withdraw from the agreement without penalty, together with the requirement that a written notice of that right be delivered in a prescribed form and sometimes in the language of negotiation. Window length, form and delivery are an obligation class that varies by jurisdiction, sale setting and contract type and must be verified currently rather than assumed.

a purchased lead sold simultaneously to several sellers versus one sold to a single buyer; sharing changes the economics through contact races, homeowner irritation and lower close rates, so exclusivity, delivery order and the number of co-buyers are contractual diligence questions before the first paid batch.

a lead delivered or resold some time after the homeowner's original enquiry; age degrades contact rate and intent independently of the seller's skill, which is why lead age at delivery is a diligence question and why a contact-rate collapse is investigated at the record before it is blamed on the caller.

a sit is an appointment the homeowner actually keeps with the decision-makers present; the sit rate is held appointments divided by appointments set, and it is the diagnostic that separates a lead-source problem from a setting-conversation problem, since a set-but-not-held appointment consumes the seller's scarcest resource and produces nothing.

total spend on a channel divided by the deals from that channel that reached installation and final payment rather than by leads or by signatures; it is the only channel-comparable cost figure in this business because it absorbs contact, sit, close and post-signature survival, and it is always paired with the cash-out to cash-in lag.

the household's month-by-month electricity use reconstructed from twelve months of billed kilowatt-hours or the utility's interval export, split across rate periods where a time-of-use schedule applies, with anomalies resolved by an explicit keep, adjust or annotate decision; a baseline built on fewer than twelve months is labelled provisional wherever it is used.

a forward change in consumption that is ordered, financed, permitted, or already installed, versus one the household merely intends; only committed changes move the base case, and aspirational ones appear only as separately labelled alternative cases.

the compass direction a roof plane faces and the angle it rises at; with latitude and shade they set how much of the available sunlight a plane can convert, and they are the first two facts recorded per candidate plane.

the share of the theoretically available annual irradiance a specific plane actually receives once obstructions are accounted for, measured on the roof with an instrument or modeled from imagery or elevation data; it enters the production model per plane and per season with its method named, never as a single eyeballed annual figure.

a rate structure pricing energy differently by hour, day type and season, so the value of a displaced or exported kilowatt-hour depends on when it happens; it is the reason a single blended cents-per-kilowatt-hour figure misstates both the pre-solar and the post-solar bill.

the rule set deciding what the utility credits for energy the array sends back - full-retail netting, a reduced export-rate or avoided-cost class, or a time-differentiated export value - together with its true-up period, its surplus treatment, and any grandfathering; it applies as of the system's interconnection, not as of a neighbour's older system.

a bill component the customer keeps paying on consumed energy regardless of how the array is credited; it is one of the reasons a post-solar bill does not fall to zero and it must be carried into the comparison rather than netted away.

the required form of any generation figure shown to a homeowner: a central estimate produced from surveyed geometry, measured shade and the equipment the installer will fit, with the modeling tool, the long-run weather dataset and every loss assumption named, presented with an uncertainty band and a weather-variance statement and never as a promise.

an escalator is a contractual clause raising a lease or power-purchase payment by a stated percentage each year of the term; a utility-escalation assumption is the modeler's assumed rate of future utility price increase applied to the do-nothing side of a comparison. They are routinely confused; the first is disclosed with its late-term payment shown, the second is sourced to published rate history or a regulator's filing and always shown beside a zero-escalation case.

glossary.term: financing classes (cash, loan, lease, power purchase agreement)
glossary.definition: the four ownership and obligation structures, distinguished by who owns the equipment, who may claim an ownership-linked incentive, whether the payment is debt service, rent for equipment, or a price per kilowatt-hour generated, who maintains and monitors, and what happens at end of term and on sale of the home; the comparison is delivered before any price.

the mechanism by which a lender offering a below-market advertised rate is compensated - a charge to the dealer or seller embedded in the installed price - which is why identical hardware carries a different sticker under a low-rate loan than under cash; its size is a per-deal fact read from the lender's schedule and the installer's pricing, never assumed.

the building or electrical department that issues the permit and performs inspection for the address; its plan-review and inspection queue is one of the timeline stages the seller does not control and must therefore describe as a range with the gating stage named.

the per-household record pairing every input a proposal uses with the dated artifact it came from - bills or usage export, rate-schedule identifier, export-rules page, shade output, roof and service-panel photographs, installer scope and price - so the proposal is auditable a year later when the household compares real bills to the estimate.

the fixed self-check run before any household is asked to sign, in which a failed item is a stop rather than a note: traceability of every number, absence of guarantee language, modeled-with-band labelling, escalation cases shown, financing class walked and restated, site risks disclosed, and no pressure device used.

the comprehension check in which the homeowner restates in their own words who they will pay, for how long, what happens if they move, and what their cancellation right is; a failed teach-back defers the signature and is never treated as an objection to handle.

the queue of sold-but-unbuilt jobs an installer carries, expressed as the depth of work ahead of a newly submitted deal; it is read from the installer's own job records by stage rather than from a quoted average, because the backlog - not the recruiting deck - sets the only timeline a seller may state.

a set of completed jobs from the same installer and roughly the same period whose stage dates - signature, survey, engineering, permit issue, install, inspection, activation - are read together so the seller sees the spread and the slow tail rather than a mean; it is the only licensed source of homeowner-facing timeline language.

what moves to the installer at signature - executed agreement and disclosures, access and scheduling constraints, utility account and roof details, known site conditions, and every commitment made at the table - paired with the seller's own dated record of the timeline range stated, the gating stage named, and what was promised.

the itemized list of unfinished or defective items identified at or after install - conduit routing, sealant, trim, debris, damaged tile, mislabelled disconnects - whose documented closure is one of the objective conditions of a verified-happy install.

a cost item appearing after the original agreement because the site requires it - a main-panel upgrade, roof repair or reroof, structural reinforcement, trenching, or a derate remedy - whose appearance changes price or scope and therefore triggers a written re-disclosure and a fresh homeowner decision before work proceeds.

the pre-agreed sequence of named contacts and response expectations inside the installer organization - coordinator, project manager, operations lead - that the seller uses in writing when a job stalls or a defect appears, and against which the partner's response behaviour is scored.

a job that has objectively cleared the conditions making advocacy honest: energized with activation granted, production visible in monitoring and consistent with the model, punch list documented closed, first post-activation statement walked through, no open service ticket or complaint, and no advocacy opt-out on file.

the measured rate at which a cohort of completed installs produces introductions, appointments and eventually installed deals over following periods, computed from the seller's own source-tagged install ledger; it is the only way to see whether reputation is actually compounding in a model with no contracted recurring revenue.

the way this specialist handles every regulatory point - naming the kind of duty and the kind of authority that issues it (home-solicitation notice, canvassing permit, do-not-knock, contact consent and registry scrub, seller-side registration, financing and third-party-ownership disclosure, referral compensation, review disclosure) together with the standing instruction to verify the current rule in the operating jurisdiction and record the check with its date - rather than asserting a specific window, form, threshold, or fee.

competency_questions_covered: What does anti-pressure, verified-numbers selling actually require me to do differently on a real appointment, and how do I keep the rules when a month-end shortfall argues against them?

Should I operate as a commissioned rep under someone else's dealer, as my own dealer contracting with an installer, or as a referral partner - and what does each choice do to my capital need, my control, and my exposure when a deal cancels?
Which licences, registrations, and permits attach to me as the seller rather than to the installer, and how do I confirm them for each town and state I sell into?
How is my commission actually computed on one deal, when does each portion of it arrive, and under what conditions can it be taken back?
Which lead channels should I run, and what does each really cost me once the deals that never reach installation are counted?
A lead vendor is pitching me volume at an attractive price - what do I verify before the first invoice, and how do I test them without betting the month on it?
My numbers dropped this month - are the leads bad, is the appointment-setting conversation bad, or is my qualification loose?
In what order do I qualify a homeowner, and what is the cheapest question that disqualifies the most bad deals earliest?
How do I find out whether a household can finance at all without pulling credit myself, storing credit data, or drifting into financial advice?
How do I recognize a homeowner for whom this commitment could do real harm, and what changes about my process when I do?

How many leads and held appointments must exist now to produce installed, fully-paid deals three months out, and how do I plan personal cash flow across that gap without letting money pressure change how I sell?
What has to be true before any number is allowed to appear in a proposal a homeowner keeps?
How do I turn a household's bills into a defensible consumption baseline, and when is last year's history the wrong baseline for next year's system?
How do I read this household's rate structure so the 'what you pay today' side of the comparison is the real bill and not a blended average?
How is exported energy compensated for a system interconnecting now, and what does that do to the value of building a bigger array?
How do I qualify a roof - planes, orientation, shade, remaining life - and which parts of that judgement are the installer's and not mine?
How do I present a production number as a model with uncertainty instead of a promise, and what would make any number a commitment?
How do I size the array when consumption, roof area, export rules, panel capacity and budget all point at different answers?
How do I build a savings comparison that still holds up when the homeowner checks it against their next twelve bills?
What are the financing classes, who owns the system in each, and what must be disclosed before a homeowner signs one?
How do I talk about tax credits, rebates and certificate programs without giving tax advice or booking them as money the homeowner is certain to get?
What actually happens between signature and the day the system is allowed to run, and how do I set that expectation without promising a date?
What is the last check that stops a defective proposal from reaching a signature, and what does the homeowner walk away holding?

How do I choose which installer to sell for when my name is the one the homeowner will remember in five years, and how do I check build quality with evidence instead of the installer's recruiting deck?
How deep is this installer's backlog really, and what timeline am I therefore allowed to state to a homeowner at the kitchen table?
What in the dealer or referral agreement actually decides when I get paid and under what conditions the money can be taken back?
Should I sell for one installer or several, and what happens to my in-flight deals and my past customers if the installer fails, exits my market, or terminates me?
At signature, what exactly moves to the installer, what record proves what the homeowner was told, and from that moment which questions are mine to answer and which are the installer's?
The site survey came back with a main-panel upgrade or a roof condition that changes the price or the scope - what must be re-disclosed, re-consented, and re-signed before anything continues?
A homeowner tells me they want to cancel - what am I allowed to do, what must I do immediately, and where does a save attempt stop being legitimate?
My commission statement shows a deduction I did not expect - how do I reconcile it and dispute it without guessing?
When is a customer actually ready to be asked for a referral or a review, and how do I ask without pressure, without hiding compensation, and without breaking platform rules?
A public complaint, a bad review, or a consumer-protection inquiry has landed on a deal I sold - what do I do first, and what am I not allowed to do?
